answer: To stop one operator from voting many times, each agent registers a CryptoNote-style key image: a public tag that a single long-term secret can produce exactly once. When that image first reaches the network harbor of new identities it is seated; any later registration that reprints the same image is dropped as a clone. Auditors walking a meadow of fresh sign-ups only compare images, never the secret, and across the ocean of established agents extra names are worthless because they cannot be backed by a second independent image.
